subject: physics
title: SHM Definition and Equations
welcome_lead: Meet a = -ω²x and the rest of SHM mathematics in one sitting.
meta_desc: A-Level SHM adventure on the defining equation and solutions for displacement, velocity and acceleration.
final_note: Velocity is zero at amplitude; acceleration is zero at equilibrium.

concepts.def: x = A cos(ωt) if starting at amplitude.

walkthroughs.body_html: SHM exists whenever acceleration is proportional to displacement from equilibrium and points back to it. Mathematically: a = −ω² x.
If released from amplitude: x = A cos(ωt). Differentiate: v = −Aω sin(ωt), a = −Aω² cos(ωt) = −ω² x.
v_max = Aω at x = 0. a_max = ω² A at x = ±A. At amplitude, v = 0; at equilibrium, a = 0.

If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.
There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
Negative acceleration means the car is moving backwards.

mcqs.q: If a car has negative acceleration, what does that necessarily mean?
options: Negative acceleration means the car is moving backwards.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
Its acceleration is in the negative direction (often opposite to the chosen positive direction); it may be slowing down or speeding up in reverse.
Negative acceleration always means the car is slowing down.

mcqs.q: What force keeps a car moving in a circle around a bend?
options: The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
A centrifugal force pushes the car outwards from the centre.
The car's own momentum acts as a force that drives it in a circle.
Friction from the road acting towards the centre of the circle — centripetal force.
